scope: Published and regulatory sources behind each deterministic safety rule. Status meanings are below; no rule is looser than its source.

statusMeaning.confirmed: The source names this ingredient and this effect.
statusMeaning.extended: The source covers a close relative; the rule applies it to this ingredient.
statusMeaning.design-choice: No source requires this rule; it is deliberately stricter than the sources.

bjd-1998-retinoid-bpo.citation: Chemical stability of adapalene and tretinoin when combined with benzoyl peroxide in presence and in absence of visible light and ultraviolet radiation. Br J Dermatol. 1998;139 Suppl 52:8-11.
bjd-1998-retinoid-bpo.finding: With benzoyl peroxide and light, tretinoin lost over 50% in about 2 hours and 95% in 24 hours.

fda-retin-a-micro-label-2025.citation: U.S. FDA. RETIN-A MICRO (tretinoin) gel prescribing information, sections 5.1 and 5.3. 2025.
fda-retin-a-micro-label-2025.finding: Concomitant OTC benzoyl peroxide, sulfur, resorcinol or salicylic acid may increase dryness, erythema and peeling; minimise UV exposure.

fda-aha.citation: U.S. FDA. Alpha Hydroxy Acids (content current as of 22 Nov 2022), with Guidance for Industry: Labeling for Topically Applied Cosmetic Products Containing Alpha Hydroxy Acids (2005).
fda-aha.finding: AHAs raised UV-induced reddening by 18% after four weeks; FDA recommends a sunburn alert. Names glycolic, lactic and citric acid.

fda-bha.citation: U.S. FDA. Beta Hydroxy Acids (content current as of 25 Feb 2022).
fda-bha.finding: Citing CIR: salicylic acid safe when formulated to avoid irritation and increased sun sensitivity; advises sun protection.

cir-aha-2017.citation: Fiume MM. Alpha Hydroxy Acids. Int J Toxicol. 2017;36(5 suppl 2):15S-21S (CIR re-review of the 1998 assessment).
cir-aha-2017.finding: Consumer AHA products safe up to 10% at pH 3.5 or above, when formulated to avoid sun sensitivity or directed with daily sun protection.

ntp-tr568.citation: National Toxicology Program. Photocarcinogenesis study of retinoic acid and retinyl palmitate in SKH-1 mice (TR-568). 2012.
ntp-tr568.finding: Retinyl palmitate and retinoic acid increased squamous cell neoplasms under simulated solar light.

npra-annex-ii-2025.citation: NPRA / ASEAN Cosmetic Directive. Annex II: list of substances which must not form part of the composition of cosmetic products. Release 2 July 2025.
npra-annex-ii-2025.finding: Entry 375 tretinoin (retinoic acid); entry 39 antibiotics; entry 300 glucocorticoids.

npra-2018-statement.citation: Director General of Health Malaysia. Press statement: cosmetic products found to contain scheduled poison. NPRA, 9 October 2018.
npra-2018-statement.finding: Hydroquinone and tretinoin are pharmaceuticals that need DCA registration and should be used only under healthcare supervision.

aicis-eva00186.citation: AICIS. Evaluation statement EVA00186: retinal (CAS 116-31-4). 26 June 2026.
aicis-eva00186.finding: Repr. 1B, H360D; no longer eligible as an exempted or reported introduction for consumer use.

npra-appendix7.citation: NPRA. Appendix 7: Special conditions for registration for a particular product or group of products, entry 4 (isotretinoin/tretinoin). Posted 29 August 2018.
npra-appendix7.finding: Isotretinoin and tretinoin may be supplied only to DCA-approved dermatologists or government hospitals with a skin specialist; labels must warn that they are highly teratogenic.

doctoroncall-differin.citation: DoctorOnCall (licensed online pharmacy, Malaysia). Differin (adapalene) 0.1% gel product page: prescription-only medicine; registration holder Galderma Malaysia Sdn Bhd. Accessed 6 November 2026.
doctoroncall-differin.finding: Adapalene 0.1% gel (Differin) is sold in Malaysia as a prescription-only medicine.

npra-otc-forum-2017.citation: NPRA. Presentation to the International Over-the-Counter Medicines Regulators Forum, 2017 (hosted by TGA).
npra-otc-forum-2017.finding: MAL suffix A = prescription (scheduled poison / controlled medicine); X = non-prescription (OTC).

differin-mal.citation: Differin 0.1% Gel (30 g), Malaysian registration number MAL20010011ARZ, product listing on newpages.com.my. Accessed 6 November 2026.
differin-mal.finding: Adapalene 0.1% gel is registered in Malaysia under MAL20010011ARZ; the A after the digits marks a prescription (scheduled poison) product.

aklief-mal.citation: Aklief Cream 50 mcg/g (trifarotene), Laboratoires Galderma, Malaysian registration number MAL24076001AZ, product listing on newpages.asia. Accessed 6 November 2026.
aklief-mal.finding: Trifarotene cream is registered in Malaysia under MAL24076001AZ; the A after the digits marks a prescription product.
